messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty -> realtime-serving-high-tail-latency fired (P3). alert_id=pgd_9982, monitors=[tail_latency, queue_depth]. Auto-escalation scheduled in 3m.
pagerduty: Duplicate alert: realtime-serving-queue-depth triggered as well — linking incidents.
maya (oncall): Acked. Looking at console now — link: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/realtime/latency?from=now-15m . Initial glance: tail p95 jumped to ~1.5s, but p50 steady. Any obvious customer impact?
jia (eng-runtime): Not seeing 5xxs on the ingress logs. Could be a transient KV cache warmup or a synthetic canary. Pulling runtime logs for the realtime model pool.
infra-bot: Autoscaler events:
- 2026-03-15T09:03:21Z scale_up pool=realtime-gpu delta=3 -> capacity=23
- 2026-03-15T09:03:49Z scale_down pool=realtime-gpu delta=-3 -> capacity=20 (stabilized)
sam (eng-sre): If it's autoscaler thrash, we might be getting spike/lag when new nodes join. Can you paste the router backpressure logs, jia? Also check redis/kvs lag.
jia (eng-runtime): Logs snippet from router at the spike:
```
[09:02:58] router: request=abc123 model=realtime-v2 seq_len=128 queue_wait_ms=842 proc_ms=12
[09:03:02] router: request=def456 model=realtime-v2 seq_len=64 queue_wait_ms=1200 proc_ms=10
[09:03:05] router: proc_pool: pool=realtime-gpu add_node start; reason=scale_up
[09:03:07] router: request=ghi789 model=realtime-v2 seq_len=256 queue_wait_ms=1500 proc_ms=15
```
This looks like a brief queue wait when the scaler kicked in. No 5xx.
maya (oncall): OK that matches the dashboard. Can we confirm whether this was traffic from synthetic canaries? Last 15m top sources show a spike from synthetic/ci-canary-1.
infra-bot: synthetic/ci-canary-1 sent 1.8k requests in a 30s window starting 09:02:50Z. Baseline is ~20 req/min.
maya (oncall): Oof — that explains it. PagerDuty: are pages still active or auto-resolving?
pagerduty: tail_latency alert auto-resolved at 09:04:12Z after metric returned below threshold. queue_depth alert auto-resolved at 09:04:30Z. Both incidents closed by auto-resolve.
sam (eng-sre): Good. We should mute the synthetic canary for a minute and tune its ramp to avoid causing autoscaler churn in the cluster. Can we pause it? @ci-team?
jia (eng-runtime): I ran a temporary rate-limit on that canary from the routing layer: `routectl apply --source synthetic/ci-canary-1 --rate 10rps` — effect immediate, verified drop in incoming qps.
maya (oncall): Command acknowledged. Thanks. Any customer-facing errors observed?
jia (eng-runtime): No 5xxs and no increase in API error rate. Token consumption bump only. All customer routes show <10ms p50 and p95 back to normal by 09:05.
sam (eng-sre): I'll follow up to add a guard: if synthetic source QPS delta > 5x baseline in 1m, block or throttle automatically to protect production capacity. Filing infra ticket IR-2026-042.
maya (oncall): Handoff to sam for 30m follow-up and to confirm the canary change and infra ticket. I'll mark this as watchers-only; no customer impact.
jia (eng-runtime): Quick note for runbook: when autoscaler causes brief queue wait, check `routectl` to identify sources, throttle synthetic origins, and check node join logs for >500ms kernel scheduling lag.
maya (oncall): Closing thread. If it repeats we'll open a postmortem — adding labels: flaky-auto-scale, synthetic-spike, no-customer-impact. Thanks all :thumbsup:
sam (eng-sre): Confirmed handoff — will monitor for 30m and follow up with infra ticket link and proposed mitigation tomorrow.
incident-bot: Incident thread archived (auto-close) — duration ~3m6s, final status: auto-resolved, no-customer-impact.
